chapter_note: Remarkably clean substrate chapter. Teaching purity 1.000 with zero editorial fatigue and zero scores for editorial_bridge, institutional, or exhortation across all paragraphs. The entire chapter (minus the one-line dialogue frame opening) is systematic cosmological teaching about the First Man's five garments (fire, wind, water, light, air) and their cosmic roles in the battle with Darkness. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system throughout. The five-element nomenclature and the process of mixture/wounding are core substrate features. The text is heavily lacunose but the teaching structure is clear.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic attribution: 'Once again our light father speaks:' — no cosmological content whatsoever. Standard dialogue frame opener.

paragraphs.core_text: When the [First] Man came forth against the ene[my ...] ⟨p.127⟩ garment [...] the Darkness with the garment of [of] living fire. With that garment he withered the tumescence (?) of the enemy; he brought down i[t]s foolery and its vanity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic process description: the First Man deploys the garment of living fire against Darkness. Both sides internal to the cosmic system — cosmic agent vs. cosmic adversary, cosmic element as weapon. Heavily lacunose but the substrate structure is clear.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, this one alone was sufficient for them. [Y]et, si[n]ce the living fire was weakened, because of this he added [to it another fou]r garments: that of the wind, that of the water, that of the light, and that of the a[i]r. And this, (why) has he given the four? He gave them s[o] th[a]t they would be helpe[r]s to t[h]at god, wh[ich i]s the living fire; so that [...] not with [in] the living f[ire], and penetrate it; and [the po]ison and the [enmi]ty cut it off.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic five-element enumeration: fire already deployed, then the four additional garments (wind, water, light, air) given as helpers. The rhetorical question 'And this, (why) has he given the four?' is a pedagogical device within the teaching tradition — it structures the explanation, not an editorial insertion. The five-element nomenclature is a core substrate marker.

paragraphs.core_text: While the fire received a bl[ow and] a wound in its body; yet still, [...] all the powers of Da[rk]ness because of it [...] It [...] necessity [...] brothers, to cause them to receive a blow and a woun[d to]o. The power of the en/emy mixed in with them. Rath[er, ex]cept [the air]. The Darkness did not mix in with it, nor was the burning of the enemy able to penet/rate it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Describes the cosmic process of mixture — fire wounded, the other elements wounded and mixed with the enemy's power, except air which remained unmixed. 'Brothers' here is cosmological kinship among the five elements, not audience address. The mixture process and the exception of air are core cosmological-process teaching. Heavily lacunose but the teaching survives.

paragraphs.core_text: Never-theless, even the one that remained behind without the wound, which is the air, it stripped off garment and power. It gave it to its [fo]ur brothers in its place; so that by that [ga]rment of the living air they would become strong, and [...] profit, and endure, namely its other four brothers. And it [be]came for them [...] life.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the cosmic process: the unwounded air sacrificially gives its garment to the wounded four, strengthening them. This is systematic cosmic-process teaching — the air's unique role in the five-element structure. The kinship language ('brothers') is cosmological, describing internal relations among the five elements. The pattern (one giving to the four) is structural substrate.
